text:
alex: Heads-up — profiler flagged a host-side CPU spike during streaming requests with many tiny chunks (~64-256B). gRPC writev syscalls are hot, tail latency jumps. Flame attached below. :eyes:

sam: Can you paste the flame/trace? curious if kernel selection or batching heuristics are misrouting small writes to slow paths.

alex: Pasted sample from perf: 
```
  35.2%  runtime          [kernel.kprobe] writev
  12.7%  host-proxy       token_parse
   8.9%  grpc             http2::writev
   7.6%  tokenizer        utf8_norm
   5.4%  host-preproc     kv_cache_miss_handler
```
Also saw lots of small writev()s: 3-8 syscalls per response.

marta: Noted we had a KV cache miss bump on the same window, +1.8% miss rate. That can amplify host CPU because parse/cold-path does more allocs.

perf-bot: Automated profile summary: peak host CPU 78% on ingress core, 95th tail latency 420ms, median 22ms. Correlation: +2% KV miss => +12% syscall overhead.

sam: Two hypotheses: (1) We accidentally switched kernel selection for small batches to a non-vectorized kernel last night; (2) batching heuristics let tiny chunks through too eagerly. Either can blow up writev frequency.

alex: I grepped logs — there was a kernel roll last deploy: kernel_picker selected kernel-id 0x3b for sequences <128 tokens. That maps to a conservative path.

emma: Also check HTTP/2 HPACK overhead vs unary gRPC stream framing. HPACK can force many small frames if headers not reused. Did we change client header usage?

marta: Quick A/B: toggled coalesce threshold from 256 -> 1024 bytes on a client-side edge proxy (local sim). Result: host CPU down ~12% and 95th tail down ~30ms. No change to model kernel path yet.

sam: Nice. That suggests IO spike is big factor. Long-term: we should (a) make kernel picker consider upstream coalesce size as a signal, (b) tighten batching heuristic to prefer slightly larger micro-batches for RPC paths, (c) add small ingress micro-delay (0.5-1ms) to allow natural coalescing of fragments.

alex: Test commands I ran: 
```
wrk -t4 -c200 -d60s --latency --script=stream-small.lua http://edge-proxy.test/stream
git rev-parse --short HEAD => 9f2c7d1
```
Observations attached in logs.

marta: Also surfaced that kv_cache eviction threshold increased slightly due to pod memory pressure earlier — that explains miss bump. I'll pin cache size on canary.

sam: I'll open a small PR to: increase coalesce threshold default to 1024, add config flag for ingress micro-delay, and add a kernel-picker telemetry metric (coalesce_size -> kernel_id mapping). Will add integrational perf test to CI that runs wrk script.

alex: For rollback criteria — revert if 95th tail increases or token CPU increases >5% after 24h.

emma: Also want a quick probe comparing HTTP/1.1 gRPC-proxy vs native http2/gRPC to rule out HPACK framing. I'll run that tomorrow.

perf-bot: Perf job scheduled: nightly/ingress-coalesce-check -> diff baseline (today) vs canary (coalesce=1024) in perf dashboard.

alex: Plan sounds good. Sam — assign PR to me once draft is up, will run canary on one node pool. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
